svg.title: One metadata pointer, two catalogs
svg.desc: UNREGISTER on catalog A returns the latest metadata location and leaves the files in the bucket. REGISTER on catalog B attaches that pointer. The 19 October 2026 Databricks post calls this Private Preview. The October product notes do not list it. DROP is a different door: a managed table is marked for deletion and can be restored with UNDROP inside a recovery window.

g.text: The files stay. The managing catalog changes.
19 October blog: REGISTER and UNREGISTER are Private Preview. Ask the account team.
October notes through 19 October, and the managed-tables page updated 8 October, do not name the calls.
A later commit on A must fail.
The bucket has to be one
The posts do not name the
B is then the only catalog
Two doors that are not this handoff
DROP on a managed table marks files for deletion. UNDROP default is 7 days. 30 days is the Public Preview ceiling, not the default.
The 11 September summary table still says an 8-day retention. The 19 October post says up to 30 days and prints no default.
SET MANAGED, on the 11 September convert page, copies a Delta table into the managed location. Iceberg is not in that list.
SET MANAGED IN PLACE, with no data movement, is a roadmap sentence on the 19 October post. The FAQ on that page already says SET MANAGED.
Stop writers and repoint jobs before the pair. The 5 October post deferred those steps. 19 October did not write them.
If REGISTER fails after UNREGISTER, the name is on neither catalog. The files are still in the bucket. No compensating call is specified.
Foreign Iceberg stays read-only until REGISTER. That call is the private preview, not a line in the October notes.
